existing_findings.status: Existing historical finding; previous current REVIEW-HAIR-TIED-AXIS-PROGRESS-95E and REVIEW-HAIR-GUIDE-MAX-PATH-95E are related current elaborations, not new unique findings here.
existing_findings.current_source_evidence: Haircut fields 146–173 and scaled 297–313 are raw f32, longest 317–319 is maximum of four public lengths. Non-Bun tied constructor 33–53 samples a two-millimetre step while s<length, pushing each point; CPU Hairdo::guides 179–227 invokes Tied::new after roots. GPU grow 100–110/118–173 invokes record_hairdo_guides; gpu/guides.rs 130–145/249–265 computes longest and max_path before packed.rs 8–23 invokes Tied::new. Earlier root placement/device work can fail first.
existing_findings.qualified_reasoning: Infinite longest can never be reached by a finite step count, and on IEEE f32 at s=65536 adjacent floats are 1/128 apart; .002 is less than half this spacing, so if the accumulator reaches that state it can stop increasing. Earlier allocation/resource failure may intervene. At GPU max_path, casting +infinity to u32::MAX then adding 2 can overflow under checked arithmetic before packed tied creation. Actual build profile, ordinary product input, loop progress, GPU behavior and errors were not run or observed.
existing_findings.future_direction: Retain coherent finite supported executable hair-length and resource policy before CPU/GPU guide paths; use checked derived counts/size arithmetic while preserving zero optional cases, signed offsets/angles and style modes. Central decides relationships between host progress and GPU count arithmetic.

nonfindings: Tied::new returns None for non-tied flow, while Bun skips the axis loop and supplies a second point if necessary; optional/nonempty fallback are explicit supported modes.
Private Tied constructor provides at least two axis nodes before frame i/i+1; the inspected factory alone does not show an empty-axis index failure.
Arrangement::tied and Hairdo::flow agree on Ponytail, Bun and Braid in the inspected cases; no second stored authority or invalid style/cut cross product is shown.
Guide count is selected from 110, 140 or 160; inspected 40-times candidate count is bounded by 6400. This does not prove scalp boundary cardinality or other GPU sizes.
Braid has its own along/lane phase and ignores the separately passed phase; Bun uses phase. These are distinct mode equations, not proof of a compatibility issue.

lenses.name: producer-propagation
lenses.assessment: Public Serde Hairdo combines follicles, haircut, style; hairdo.flow selects tie mode. CPU guides and GPU packed host preparation both call Tied::new; GPU first computes max_path. Selected creator shape scales preset haircut and adjusts style before its own look enters downstream paths.

lenses.name: existing-type-owners
lenses.assessment: Arrangement owns closed authored style, Haircut owns authored cut/length, Hairdo combines them, and private Flow/Tie/Tied derive integration and head-relative axis. These owners carry different roles rather than duplicate competing styles.

lenses.name: admission-contracts
lenses.assessment: Style and cut contain public f32 values, ordinary Serde and no assigned-body accepted-value gate. Existing rig F067 addresses executable hair length/progress; checked creator ShapeValues and NaN-preserving with_knobs remain separate F017.

lenses.name: invariant-operations
lenses.assessment: Non-Bun tied axis increments f32 s by .002 while s<raw longest; unbounded/nonfinite length lacks a progress/work certificate. GPU longest→cast→u32 max+2 is an earlier distinct conditional arithmetic point. Both are part of historical F067 and previous current reviews.

lenses.name: aggregate-states
lenses.assessment: Tied::new guarantees axis at least two elements before frame indexes i/i+1; input hairstyle, cut, head and axis must still satisfy connected geometric and numerical conditions. Duplicate F067 work is not counted.

lenses.name: type-ownership
lenses.assessment: Arrangement, cut, follicles and private flow/tie are distinct producer/consumer stages, and a tied axis is a derived geometry product. Shared signed offsets, lengths and unitful angles require context-aware ownership.

lenses.name: redundant-authority
lenses.assessment: Arrangement::tied, Hairdo::flow and matches! expose related projections of one enum; no inconsistent mapping found in inspected ten cases, and a stored second authored state is not established.

lenses.name: behavior-preservation
lenses.assessment: Assigned files individually match historical 6533 and pinned current 95e. This does not establish a clean pr-working tree, full source-graph equality, rendering or product behavior.

lenses.name: enum-shapes
lenses.assessment: Natural/Parted/etc and three tied modes remain distinct; non-tied Tied::new None and Bun two-node fallback are supported states. Hairstyle.cut/growth/style independence is explicit; no blanket combination constraint.

lenses.name: derivability
lenses.assessment: Assigned style derives standard Serialize/Deserialize and standard traits; Tied intentionally has internal geometry, no additional derive substitution was proven.

lenses.name: type-granularity
lenses.assessment: Style part and lift/tuck/tie are signed positions or angles; hold/cling/volume are lengths, scalp shape and relative hair lengths have independent contracts. Do not treat all floats as probability or require a uniform positive-only value.

lenses.name: magic-strings
lenses.assessment: Arrangement.name returns human display labels while serde snake_case is a distinct typed encoding. No raw string-valued style selector or retained string protocol in the assigned sources is established.

lenses.name: magic-numbers
lenses.assessment: Two millimetre axis step, index interpolation, braid/bun geometry coefficients and finite preset defaults are local geometric behavior. Progress, total allocation and native max-path bounds are separate questions from replacing literals with wrappers.
